page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is a compute-focused general virtual machine instance driven by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 physical cores mapped to 4 dedicated vCPUs with single threading per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes a local 161 GB SSD drive and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier execution for standard raw compute and mixed results across memory-bound tests. The instance achieves average throughput in stress-ng evaluations, registering 1,822.38 in single-core and 7,232.57 in multi-core routines, alongside standard large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 49.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 30.16 GB/sec. Conversely, Geekbench 6 returns lower-tier scores of 1,112.0 single-core and 3,670.0 multi-core, with PassMark memory testing and cryptographic instruction benchmarks falling into the lower quartile.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 memory configuration prioritizes execution logic density over massive in-memory caching. The local 161 GB solid-state disk provides fast scratch space directly attached to the host, bypassing network-attached storage latency for ephemeral needs. The ARM Neoverse-N1 cores provide stable per-core execution without hyper-threading contention, though workloads requiring x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX or AVX-512 are unsupported.

The D4plds_v5 instance is practical for ARM-native continuous integration and build pipelines, lightweight web microservices, batch processing, and caching tiers that fit comfortably within an 8.0 GB footprint. The combination of dedicated ARM physical cores and low-latency local SSD makes it suitable for cost-conscious, compute-skewed distributed workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by a 4-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz with dedicated single-threaded execution. The configuration provides 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, complemented by 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage without integrated GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates mid-tier performance in raw stress-ng multi-core workloads and large-block memory transfers, while displaying weaker metrics in Geekbench and PassMark instruction evaluations. The reduced memory footprint relative to core count shifts the resource profile toward compute tasks rather than data-heavy caching. Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is suited for ARM64 application builds, distributed web services, lightweight containerized workloads, and batch jobs requiring fast local scratch storage without expansive memory overhead.
